findings.summary: Modulation recording computed its clean base with a weaker evaluator than playback — blind to postBehavior, defaulting isLog to false, and using a narrower rotation predicate — so recorded keyframes were baked against a base the timeline never plays.
findings.change: Replaced the evaluateTrackValue(keys, frame, id.includes('rotation')) call with animationEngine.evaluateTrack(track, frame), the public side-effect-free evaluator documented as matching playback on all three axes. The call site already had the full Track in hand. Dropped the now-unused import; left a comment recording the one remaining gap (evaluateTrack skips the evaluatePairedTrack step scrub() tries first, so camera-pair tracks can still differ slightly).
findings.verification: An independent verifier that had not seen the auditor's reasoning re-derived all three divergences from source and measured each with a tsx probe against the real interpolators. ROTATION: the two predicates disagree on 33 of the 443 real modulation targets (from test:modulation-coverage's live list) — droste.rotate/rotateSpin/rotatePolar (DEGREES, -360..360), coloring.twist/twistArms/twist2/twistArms2, and lighting.light0-7_rot{X,Y,Z}. Measured on a 0.1 -> 6.0 track at frame 50: recording 3.05 vs playback -0.0916 (playback applies the 2*pi shortest-path wrap; recording does not). coloring.phase/phase2 span < pi so they are dead. POSTBEHAVIOR: evaluateTrackValue takes a Keyframe[] and so structurally cannot see it; it hard-clamps. Measured past a last key at frame 50, evaluated at 75: Hold agrees (10/10), Loop and PingPong play 5, Continue and OffsetLoop play 15 — recording bakes 10 for all four. Settable from a shipped right-click menu (Graph Editor -> Extrapolation) on ANY track. ISLOG: real but inert — registerLogTrack has exactly one shipping call site (fluid-toy julia.zoom) and that target's modulation is display-only, so no log divergence is user-visible today. Verifier confidence high; it tried three refutations and failed on all three. Guards after the change: test:modulation-parity, test:modulation-coverage, test:modulated-setter, test:param-mapping, smoke:anim-play, smoke:anim-orbit, smoke:track-binding, typecheck — all pass.

findings.summary: The @invariant 'Bezier is NOT applied on log tracks' is false — AnimationMath.interpolate solves Bezier keys in (frame, log(v)) space, so tangent y-values on a log track are log-units; the same false claim was mirrored in two more source files.
findings.change: Rewrote three doc sites to state the real contract (log tracks evaluate in log-value space, Bezier included; tangent y = log-units; calculateTangents takes the matching isLog). Added an @invariant on logTrackRegistry naming the tangent-authoring callers that do NOT thread isLogTrack, so the gap is greppable. Removed the dead solveBezierY import from AnimationEngine.ts.
findings.verification: Executed a tsx probe importing engine/math/AnimationMath.ts directly: endpoints 1.0 -> 1e-6 over 100 frames, Bezier keys with flat (ease) tangents vs Linear keys, both isLog=true. Frame 10 linear-in-log 2.51e-1 vs bezier 6.76e-1 (dLog 0.989), frame 25 dLog 1.281, frame 75 dLog -1.281, frame 90 dLog -0.989. Equal ONLY at frame 50 — the auditor's first check used frame 50 and produced a false 'invariant holds', so the check was moved off-centre. Corroborated by commit 05eb7849's own message ('handles linear AND Bezier in log space (tangent y-values as log-units)') and by TrackUtils.ts:14 ('bezier-on-log evaluator'). The dead-import half is guarded by typecheck, which fails if the symbol were actually referenced.

findings.summary: smoke:binder-registry collected storePowerAfterCustom and never asserted on it, so its headline claim ('explicit registered binder OVERRIDES the DDFS auto-path') was unproven, and AnimationEngine.getBinder's registry-before-cache @invariant had no coverage at all.
findings.change: Added three assertions: store value during the custom-binder scrub must differ from the auto-path value; the auto-path value must equal what the custom writer received; and a new phase that registers a binder AFTER the DDFS auto-path has cached a writer for that id, then scrubs — asserting the late binder fires and the store does not move.
findings.verification: Falsification, not just a green run. Ran the strengthened smoke on correct code: passes (lateWrites=1, lateValue=35, storePowerAfterLate=24.5). Then inverted getBinder's order so this.binders is checked before binderRegistry.lookup, re-ran, and it failed with the intended message ('binder registered AFTER the DDFS auto-path never fired (lateWrites=0)', store showing 35 — the cached DDFS writer won). Reverted; git diff confirms only the doc/import hunks remain; smoke green again.

findings.summary: The assertion labelled 'absent axis fills with 0' contradicts readLiveVec's @invariant (absent axes fall back to base, NOT 0) and passed only because it never passed a base — the regression the invariant documents was uncovered.
findings.change: Relabelled the no-base case honestly, then added base-passing coverage: vec2 with base {x:-0.7,y:0.27} asserts the unmodulated axis keeps 0.27 rather than 0; vec3 with one modulated axis asserts the other two stay on base (the 'Y and Z jump to the origin' bug the invariant describes); plus additive-mode coverage.
findings.verification: Falsification. 18/18 assertions pass on correct code. Then changed trackBinding.ts:112 so absent axes map to 0 instead of baseAxis[i] — the exact regression the @invariant guards — and re-ran: failed with 'UNmodulated axis keeps the base value, NOT 0'. All pre-existing assertions still passed under that regression, confirming the gap was real. Reverted (git diff empty), re-ran green.

findings.summary: The header and @invariant describe four GMT composite branch bodies gated on storeState.geometry/coloring/lighting and 'the chain below switches on routing.branch' — none of that is in this file any more; the branch bodies moved to engine/features/modulation/applyTarget.ts under ADR-0109.
findings.change: Rewrote the header and @invariant to match the code, named what this file actually owns (uniform emission via FRACTAL_EVENTS, ownership tracking, liveModulations publication, keyframe capture + back-fill, accumulation-reset diff) and where the slice-gated GMT branches now live. Dropped the 'FUTURE REFACTOR — branch registry' block, since that extraction has happened.
findings.verification: Grep proves the drift: storeState.(geometry|coloring|lighting) returns only the comment lines; routing.branch only the comment. The real dispatch is planModulationTarget with the switch in applyTarget.ts:120, where the slice gating survives. test:modulation-parity independently asserts the corrected claim ('AnimationSystem.tsx dispatches via planModulationTarget') and would fail if this file went back to carrying its own chain.

findings.summary: The rule cited 'ADRs 0015-0017 (binders, recording, log/camera-pair tracks)' — ADR-0017 is the render-pipeline async-convergence ADR, ADR-0016 is deterministic playback (not recording), and no binder ADR exists at all.
findings.change: Replaced the range with per-ADR titles verified against docs/adr/ filenames, added ADR-0107/0109 for the modulation dispatch that hangs off the ANIMATE tick, stated explicitly that binderRegistry's contract is its JSDoc rather than an ADR, and added three grep-checkable invariants (registry-before-cache, Bezier-on-log, branch-bodies-not-here).
findings.verification: Every citation checked against the filesystem. ls docs/adr/ confirms 0001/0002/0003/0004/0015/0016/0107/0109 exist; head -6 on 0017 shows its Scope is engine/RenderPipeline.ts; ls docs/adr | grep -i binder returns nothing. Pre-existing citations re-verified too: engine/TickRegistry.ts, engine/plugins/RenderLoop.tsx, GmtRendererTickDriver.tsx, engine-gmt/animation/**, docs/policy/ddfs-string-contract.md all exist, and grep confirms RenderLoop.tsx:44 is still the only runTicks caller under engine/**. Each new invariant is proven by another finding in this cycle.

findings.summary: The @invariant 'Out-of-range during pause clears deck ownership' describes behaviour the code has never had — ownership is cleared by the playing→paused transition, unconditionally on range.
findings.change: Restated the invariant to match the `if (justPaused && ownedDecks.has(deckIndex))` branch: the transition clears ownership regardless of range; steady-state pause and out-of-range alone never do.
findings.verification: The single ownedDecks.delete sits behind `justPaused && ownedDecks.has(deckIndex)` — inRange is not consulted; the only other paused-branch statement is a justScrubbed/owned/inRange seek that clears nothing. git show f156dccc (the commit that added the branch, 2026-05-08) documents the intent as 'just paused (was playing) -> pause owned deck; release ownership' with no range clause, while git log -S dates the wrong invariant to 778534b0, the 2026-05-20 doc audit. The code never matched the annotation.

findings.summary: Tangent authoring omitted the isLog flag in two places despite having the track id in scope. CONFIRMED by an independent verifier, which also established the far larger live half of the problem in utils/CurveFitting.ts.
findings.change: Threaded isLogTrack(t.id) into both calculateTangents and TrackUtils.updateNeighbors. Behaviour-neutral today (no GMT camera track is log-registered) but closes the trap. Rewrote the logTrackRegistry @invariant, which named this as one of two unthreaded callers and would otherwise have become a ghost; promoted the remaining caller to @bug PRODUCTION: with the measured cost.
findings.verification: The verifier enumerated all six calculateTangents call sites: four thread the flag (timelineUtils x2, sequenceSlice, TrackUtils), two did not (CurveFitting.reTangentBezier, cameraBinders). It measured the cost with three tsx probes against the real modules: on the Bias path, authoring the same keys both ways and evaluating through interpolate(isLog=true) diverges by up to 1.34 decades (22x) on a 24-decade track, 1.20 decades on a 30-decade track, and 0.30 decades (2x) on an everyday 6-decade zoom; auto-tangent magnitudes collapse to 39%/2.2%/1.1e-17% of correct, so curves degenerate toward flat. It confirmed cameraBinders is latent (its six hardcoded ids are camera.unified.* and camera.rotation.*, none log-registered) and that CurveFitting is live (fluid-toy's julia.zoom is registered visible and IS plotted/editable in the graph editor, which has four isLogTrack branches precisely for it; nothing downstream re-tangents). Verifier confidence high. The CurveFitting half was NOT applied — see PROPOSALS.md.

findings.summary: reTangentBezier authors tangents without isLog, so the Pencil tool and the graph editor's Bias handle write linear-space tangents onto log tracks that the evaluator reads as log-units. Confirmed live, but the fix is a five-file signature change entangled with a second, larger defect.
findings.rationale: See PROPOSALS.md for the full paste-ready spec and the second defect (GraphEditor's Douglas-Peucker epsilon in linear value units).

findings.summary: ADR-0015's Decision and Consequences state Bezier is NOT supported on log tracks — the code has supported it since the ADR's own subject commit. Needs an append-only Update block; the run is not permitted to edit ADRs.
findings.rationale: See PROPOSALS.md for the paste-ready Update block.

findings.summary: smoke:anim-orbit failed once in five runs with 'Execution context was destroyed' at its first page.evaluate — the fixed waitForTimeout(2500) after waitUntil:'domcontentloaded' races a reload, and when it loses, all six real assertions are skipped.
findings.rationale: Observed once, when anim-orbit ran third in a back-to-back sequence; three solo runs and one later sequenced run passed. It fails loudly (exit 1) rather than silently, so it is a flake, not a blind spot. The same prologue appears in smoke-anim-play.mts, smoke-anim-vec2.mts and smoke-binder-registry.mts, so any of them can lose the same race. OPTIONS: (a) leave it — one-in-five under back-to-back sequencing, and it fails loudly; (b) replace the fixed sleep with a waitForFunction on window.__store / window.useAnimationStore in all four, which removes the arbitrary constant but does not close the window between the check and the next evaluate; (c) wrap the first evaluate in a single retry, which addresses the actual failure. RECOMMENDATION: (c) across all four. Not applied because the failure could not be reproduced on demand, so the fix could not be proven — and an unverifiable fix to a guard is worse than a known flake. The reproduction lever is running the four browser smokes back-to-back in one shell rather than individually.

findings.summary: _resetAudioClipSync is exported solely as a test seam and has zero callers, though the file's own @invariant says 'Tests must call _resetAudioClipSync() between cases'.
findings.rationale: grep finds the identifier only at its definition and in the comment referring to it. knip does not flag it (the config reports unused files, not unused exports). Deletion is off-limits to the run. OPTIONS: (a) keep it — three lines, documents the module's HMR-persistent-globals hazard, and is exactly what a future audioClipSync test would need; (b) delete it and the sentence referencing it; (c) write the test it was built for. RECOMMENDATION: (a) now, (c) if audio-clip sync ever regresses — syncAudioClips has genuinely testable transition logic (justResumed / justScrubbed / justPaused, the SCRUB_JUMP_SEC threshold, deck ownership) and no guard covers any of it today, which is the larger gap. Do not spend a session on (b).

notes:
All 13 files in the context:cost bundle read in full, plus engine/math/AnimationMath.ts, engine/BezierMath.ts, engine/algorithms/TrackUtils.ts and the relevant parts of utils/timelineUtils.ts, utils/CurveFitting.ts and engine/features/modulation/applyTarget.ts. Note AnimationMath.ts is not in context:cost's e03 bundle but is the interpolator named in the subsystem description and no subsystem claims engine/math — the auditor took it. All 14 @invariant annotations were checked; 4 were false or drifted, the rest verified correct — including the AnimationEngine connect() no-op, the non-float-track drop, the ignoreCamera formula plus its unconditional camera.position/camera.offset carve-out, the cameraPairRegistry DD-cache dual invalidation, and the audioFileCache 0|1 typing.

OUT-OF-LANE DRIFT for whoever owns modulation: engine/features/modulation/targetRouting.ts's @invariant says 'classifyModulationTarget must mirror the branch order in AnimationSystem.tick's per-target loop EXACTLY' and its header lists 'AnimationSystem.tick (where an offset is sent)' as a consumer. Both predate ADR-0109 — the branch chain now lives in applyTarget.ts's planModulationTarget, which is what must mirror the routing. Same drift shape as the AnimationSystem header finding, one module over.

NOT COVERED: no behavioural audit of the DD-precision camera-pair math (evaluateDDPairAxis's two-sum/Veltkamp implementation) — arithmetically dense, no dedicated guard, and verifying it properly needs a numerical probe against a known-good reference rather than a reading pass. Also, the verifier flagged that AnimationEngine.evaluateTrack is not a perfect stand-in for the full playback path: scrub() tries evaluatePairedTrack FIRST for camera-pair tracks, so camera-pair targets still diverge slightly in recording even after the applied fix. Recorded at the call site; worth a follow-up.

Two temporary code inversions were made and reverted during the audit, each to falsify a guard (getBinder lookup order, trackBinding absent-axis fallback). Both reverts confirmed clean by git diff.
